title: Synthesis of the amb-plus focus: AMB+ gives size control but no motion; NRCH gives established swimmers that a chemostat freezes into a crystal; no route to persistent division yet
summary: One page on what c08 established and found in Active Model B+ and nonreciprocal Cahn-Hilliard worlds. Established: NRCH swimmers (SIM). Submitted: the AMB+ positive control, morphology control by the sign of the active terms, NRCH flocking, and a traveling swimmer crystal under a strong chemostat. Negative: NRCH division across 18 runs, turnover in the crystal (vacancies refill by nucleation), and single-field AMB+ motility. Proposed next: a chemostat background outside the spinodal, an adsorbed boundary layer on the swimmers, and a comparison with c11's dividing nematic rods.
